title: feat(spec,service-automation,lint)!: a notify node's computed values are value slots and its link a text slot — a CEL envelope or a literal, the {…} token refused (#19939 pass 4, S4)
body:
Part of #19939
Clause-②: yes (narrowing: a {…} token is refused at notify recipients (the value or a list entry), templateData values, sourceId, actionUrl, sourceObject, actorId and any string of a payload value, a templateData value that names a dialect must be a valid CEL value envelope, and a CEL value envelope written as a payload value is refused; widening: recipients and sourceId accept a CEL value envelope they refused, a recipients list accepts envelope entries, and their published JSON Schema and inferred types gain the envelope arm)

> **Held out of the merge queue** by #22949 (the queue-wide suite-duration ceiling red; the only red on this head). Accepted, reviewed at tier (PASS 6118681762); the seat lands it when #22949 resolves.

Pass 4, stage S4 of #19939 (stage plan `6096263424`, claim `6114980625`), under ruling D on #11182 and ADR-0032 Decisions 2 and 3. A `notify` node's computed values become value slots: `recipients` (the value, or each entry of a list), `sourceId` and the values of `templateData` take a CEL value envelope the executor evaluates in the run's scope, or a literal written as it is. Its link, `actionUrl`, becomes a text slot with `{{ }}` holes, like `title`. Its `sourceObject`, `actorId` and `payload` are literals, read as written (round 2, below). A single-brace `{…}` token at any of them is refused. The family finding is fixed and pinned: a list-valued recipient entry adds each of its recipients, where the template handed it on as one joined recipient. #19939 stays open for stages S5 to S7, so this PR uses `Part of`.

## Round 2: the open question answered B (seat order `6117306001`)

The round-1 report asked whether `sourceObject`, `actorId` and `payload`, which no flow computed (zero `{…}` tokens in this repository and in hotcrm), should be value slots or literals. The seat answered B in comment `6117306001`, by the dispatch's own Zone 2 rule ("Do not build a slot nobody computes", with S7's connector inputs as the model). This round's diff, `fc5982615c..c200819d1e`:

- **The contract.** `sourceObject` and `actorId` are `z.string()` again and `payload` is `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())`: their 17.x published shapes, with no envelope arm and no marker. The contract's `superRefine` refuses a `{…}` token in `sourceObject`, in `actorId` and in any string of a `payload` value at any depth, and an envelope written as a `payload` value, with the literal's remedy, for example: "`sourceObject` is the name of the object the notification links to, a literal the executor reads as written: a single-brace token is not resolved here; write the value." An envelope at `sourceObject` or `actorId` is refused by the string type, with the same lead.
- **The build doors.** Their value arm (`builtinValueJudged`) leaves a token-carrying value alone, because only the interpolation decides what the run sees there. At a literal, the run reads what the build reads. So the contract marks these issues `readAsWritten` (`READ_AS_WRITTEN_PARAM`, in the package-internal `flow-template-token.ts`, which adds no public export; `check:api-surface` is unchanged), and the arm reports them. `FlowSchema.parse`, `objectstack validate`, the save door and `registerFlow` refuse them in the contract's words, as the executor's parse does.
- **The ledger and the executor.** The ledger drops the three rows `payload.*`, `sourceObject` and `actorId`. The executor reads the three as written; `resolveStringSlot` keeps `sourceId` only. The descriptor's help strings are restated.
- **The lint.** At a notify literal, the `flow-double-brace-interpolation` and `flow-bare-dollar-ref` hints now say that neither brace dialect resolves there, and they name the value itself. Before, they prescribed `{var}`, which the build now refuses there. The three keys are a local set in `lint-flow-patterns.ts`, pinned in step with the contract both ways.
- **The text that moves with it.** The D3 entry's surface, replacement, reason and acceptance criteria name the literals. The changeset's FROM / TO and "Newly accepted" lines are rewritten, it gains a "Newly refused at the literals" line, and its `Clause-②` line (read through `clause2-line.mjs`) drops `sourceObject` and `actorId` from the widening arm and adds the payload envelope to the narrowing arm. The generated reference and the dropped-refinements ledger move with it: `automation/NotifyConfig` loses `actorId` and `sourceObject`, 713 → 711.
- **`main`** was merged through `os-regen-merge.sh` (`fc5982615c`, from base `85b4ac634e`). It reconciled nothing, and the reference was regenerated after the change.

## What lands

**The contract (`@objectstack/spec`).**
- `NotifyConfigSchema.recipients` takes a string (one recipient as written), a list whose entries are strings or CEL value envelopes, or one envelope. It is a union, like `screen.recordId`'s, so the published JSON Schema and inferred type keep the literal arms. A value that is none of these is refused with a sentence naming what `recipients` is, and the entry at fault.
- `sourceId` takes a string or an envelope (the same union shape). `templateData` takes `FlowValueSlotSchema` per key, like a screen's `defaults`.
- A `{…}` token in any of their strings is refused by the one value-slot judge (`valueSlotTemplateRefusals`), naming its CEL spelling. A malformed envelope leads with `VALUE_ENVELOPE_REFUSAL`.
- `sourceObject`, `actorId` and `payload` are literals (round 2): their 17.x types, and a token or an envelope there refused with the literal's remedy.
- `actionUrl` stays `z.string()`, and the contract's `superRefine` refuses a single-brace token through the one text-slot judge (`textSlotTemplateRefusal`), as for `title` / `message`.
- Every `describe()` of these keys is restated.

**The ledger.**
- `FLOW_NODE_EXPRESSION_PATHS` appends three `notify` value rows: `recipients`, `templateData.*`, `sourceId`.
- `recipients` carries a new optional field, `eachElement`: the slot holds one value or a list of them, and both walks (`resolveFlowNodeExpressions`, `resolveFlowNodeValueSlots`) emit each element of a list at its own index (`recipients[1]`). An envelope entry is validated and evaluated where it sits, and a token in a string entry is refused with the envelope at its place, not as a string inside a literal.
- `NotifyConfigSchema` joins `LEDGER_DECLARED_NODE_CONFIG_SCHEMAS`: the descriptor offers these keys with no marker (the Studio form keeps its recipients picker and text inputs), so the markers ride the spec Zod channel, one slot one channel.
- `FLOW_NODE_TEXT_SLOTS` gains `notify.actionUrl`, so `registerFlow` and `objectstack validate` judge it and compile its holes, as for the other text slots.

**The judges at the doors.**
- `flowNodeValueTemplateRefusals` reaches the three positions through the ledger with no new judge. At `recipients` (the value or an entry) a refused whole token's remedy ends with the recipient sentence: an envelope that evaluates to `null` or a blank string adds no recipient, as a token that resolved to nothing did, and one that evaluates to a list adds each of its recipients.
- The build doors' value arm (`flowNodeConfigRefusals`) judges a list slot per element: an issue at an envelope entry is the envelope pass's, and a list whose every entry is a string or envelope-shaped is refused there only for a token or a malformed envelope, which their own judges report. A literal the contract refuses (`[42]`) stays this arm's.

**The executor (`@objectstack/service-automation`).**
- `notify` resolves `recipients` through `resolveRecipients`: each envelope (the whole value or an entry) through the shared `resolveValueSlot` in the run's scope; a list it evaluates to adds each recipient; `null` and a blank string add none; anything else (a map, a number, a list holding one) fails the node, naming what it evaluated to and its source, never `String(value)`.
- A node left with no recipient fails, naming the value expressions that evaluated to nothing (`framework#3582`'s guard, restated for CEL).
- `sourceId` resolves through `resolveValueSlot` and must evaluate to a string; `null` leaves the key unset; a half-specified click-through pair is still dropped. `sourceObject`, `actorId` and `payload` are read as written.
- `templateData` resolves through `resolveValueSlotMap`, like every value-slot map.
- `actionUrl` renders through `renderTextSlot`. A link that renders no text is no link, so the synthesized one still applies downstream, as an empty one did, and an explicit one still wins.
- `notify-node.ts` no longer imports `interpolate`. The descriptor's descriptions are restated; its `type`s are unchanged (the form's controls).

**The lint (`@objectstack/lint`, patch).** The `flow-double-brace-interpolation` hints name `actionUrl` among the text slots, and the dialect comment no longer lists `recipients` as single-brace. `objectstack validate` refuses the positions through the shared judges and the contract, with no rule change. At a notify literal, both wrong-syntax hints name the value itself (round 2).

**ADR-0087.** The step-18 D3 entry `18.flow-value-slot-template-dialect-refused` is amended the S1–S3 way: its surface widens to the notify positions, and its replacement, reason and acceptance criteria say what a recipient evaluates to, that a list adds each recipient and `null` none, why the list token is not rewritten, and that a literal takes the value itself. The two text-slot entries, `18.flow-text-slot-single-brace-refused` and `18.flow-text-slot-unbound-dollar-root-refused`, widen their surface to `actionUrl`, and `STEP18_RATIONALE`'s text-slot fragment (`registry.ts.template`) names the link. `registry.ts` is generated at build and gitignored. The changeset marker is `not-required (already-registered …)` naming the three ids; `check-adr-0087-registration` accepts it.

## Premises measured at the base `9fdb12752c`

Measured through the shipped `AutomationEngine` (`installBuiltinNodes`, `registerFlow`, `execute`, a recording messaging service) with a throwaway probe on the base tree, deleted after the run.

- **Today's contract.** `NotifyConfigSchema` (`io-node-config.zod.ts:274`–`:353`): `recipients` was `z.union([z.string(), z.array(z.string())])`, required; `sourceObject`, `sourceId`, `actorId`, `actionUrl` were `z.string()`; `templateData` and `payload` were `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())`. `title` / `message` were the only text slots (`templateExpressionInput`, refused a single brace since #22110).
- **The executor's readers** (`notify-node.ts`): `interpolate` ran on `recipients` (`:269`, then `toStringList`), the `templateData` values (`:291`), `actionUrl` (`:298`, then `String(…)`), the `payload` values (`:301`), `sourceObject` / `sourceId` (`:128`–`:129`, then `toStr`) and `actorId` (`:309`). `template` (`:289`), `channels` (`:293`), `topic` (`:294`) and `severity` (`:295`) were read raw. The PM's line numbers held.
- **How the doors reached them.** `flowNodeConfigRefusals` parses `NotifyConfigSchema` at `FlowSchema.parse`, `objectstack validate`, `compile`, the save door and `registerFlow` (the contract map entry, `flow-node-config-refusals.ts:125`). Its value arm skips any value carrying a `{token}`, so a token at these keys passed every door; an envelope at the four string-typed keys was refused (measured: `registerFlow` refused `recipients: { dialect: 'cel', … }` and `sourceId: { dialect: 'cel', … }`). No ledger row or judge read these keys.
- **`toStringList` (`:70`)**, measured:

| `recipients` | delivered audience |
|:--|:--|
| `'u1'` | `['u1']` |
| `'u1,u2'` | `['u1,u2']`: a string is one recipient, never split |
| `['u1', 'u2']` | `['u1', 'u2']` |
| `['{owners}']`, `owners = ['u1', 'u2']` | **`['u1,u2']`, the run succeeds**: the family finding holds |
| `'{owners}'`, the same list | `['u1', 'u2']` |
| `['{obj}']`, `obj` a record | `['[object Object]']`, the run succeeds |
| `['{missing}', 'u1']` | `['u1']`: the unresolved token is dropped |
| `['{missing}']` | `NODE_FAILURE`, "every recipient template resolved to nothing: {missing}", with the `expand` hint |

- **The other readers**, measured: `actionUrl: '{obj}'` (a map) sent the link `[object Object]`; `'/x/{when}'` with a `Date` sent `/x/"2026-10-08T09:30:00.000Z"` (JSON-quoted); `'/x/{{ id }}'` became `/x/{42}`; `'{missing}'` sent `url: ''`, and the synthesized link applied. `sourceId: '{obj}'` sent the id `[object Object]`, and `'{missing}'` dropped the pair. `templateData: { a: '{missing}' }` dropped the key, and `templateData: { a: { dialect: 'cel', … } }` handed the template the envelope object.
- **CEL, the same inputs** (`evaluateValueEnvelope`): an absent variable throws `Unknown variable: owner`; `record.owner.manager` on a scalar `owner` throws `No such key: manager`; its step-by-step `has(vars.…)` guard answers `null`; `'team:' + owner` with `owner` `null` throws `no such overload`.
- **The D2 question: D3 only.** No spelling maps losslessly. `{x}` to `x` at a recipient: an absent `x` was dropped by the template and fails the run under CEL; a list token written as a list entry reached nobody and now reaches each recipient; a record token became `[object Object]` and now fails the node. At `sourceId` an absent value dropped the link and fails the run under CEL. At a `templateData` / `payload` key an absent value dropped the key, and the guarded form writes `null`. At `actionUrl`, `{x}` to `{{ x }}` renders a `Date` and a whole-token object differently (the #22110 measurement, repeated here). So the three step-18 D3 entries are amended and no conversion is registered.
- **`#22875`** (the `template` describe) landed during this stage; `main` was merged through `os-regen-merge.sh` and the one generated path it rewrote was regenerated (below). `template` is untouched here.

## The classification

One row per key the executor read through `interpolate`, with the token census in shipped metadata and hotcrm (the reach below).

| key | S4 | census of `{…}` tokens | why |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `recipients` | value slot, one value or a list; a list-valued entry is **flattened** | showcase 16, todo 2, docs 6, dogfood 1; hotcrm 19 nodes; the objectui picker writes `{record.FIELD}` | the highest-pull computed value |
| `templateData.*` | value slot per key | docs 1; hotcrm 35 values in 19 maps | a template's per-run data |
| `sourceId` | value slot (a string) | showcase 7, todo 2, dogfood 2 | the record the link opens |
| `sourceObject` | **literal** (round 2), read as written | 0 (every site writes a literal object name) | no flow computes it |
| `actorId` | **literal** (round 2), read as written | 0 | no flow computes it |
| `payload.*` | **literal** (round 2), read as written | 0 | no flow computes it |
| `actionUrl` | text slot, `{{ }}` | showcase 4 links with holes; hotcrm 19 | the plan's carry line: a link is text |

**Flattened, not refused.** An entry that evaluates to a list adds each of its recipients. The list is what the author meant (a multi-user field, a team's members, a list variable), the whole-value form already meant a list, and the designer's one-row-per-field picker has no other way to address a multi-user field; refusing it would force every such flow into one hand-written CEL list concatenation. Nested lists, maps and numbers are refused at the node, so a flattened entry can never be a phantom recipient. Pinned (`notify-value-slots.test.ts` 3).

**The three zero-census keys are literals** (round 2). Round 1 built them as value slots and reported the choice as an open question. The seat answered B (`6117306001`) by the dispatch's own rule: no slot is built that nobody computes. Each of them resolved a token in 17.x, so a `{…}` there is refused with the literal's remedy, not forwarded verbatim.

## The reach

Re-derived at HEAD with a census of every token-bearing string at the seven positions, in `examples/**`, `packages/platform-objects`, `packages/qa/dogfood` and `content/docs/**` (references and releases excluded). Positive control: the base read 41 token strings in 7 files (`recipients` 25, `sourceId` 10, `actionUrl` 4, `templateData` 1, counted by hand for the one map the scan's object regex cuts), and HEAD reads 0.

- **Migrated in this PR:**
  - `examples/app-showcase` (`automation/flows/index.ts`): 16 recipient strings, 7 `sourceId`s and 4 links. A recipient field that may be unset (`assignee`, `owner`, `watcher`, all optional text fields) is guarded, `has(record.assignee) ? record.assignee : null`, so an unset one is dropped as the template dropped it and the node fails as before; `ownerId` (a subflow input) and the ids are plain. The urgent-task alert's two entries are guarded each, and its comment now says what it does: both are notified, and the node fails only when both are absent. The seed's comment and the stale `{record.project.owner}` / `{record.account.owner}` comments follow.
  - `examples/app-todo` (`flows/task.flow.ts`): 2 recipients (guarded) and 2 `sourceId`s.
  - Docs: `automation/flows.mdx` (the value-slot list, a new paragraph on recipients, the text-slot list, the dialect table, three samples), `automation/email-templates.mdx` (the sample and the `templateData` sentence), `getting-started/common-patterns.mdx` (two samples). The service-automation README's dialect table.
  - Dogfood: `seed-ownership-claim-dispatch.dogfood.test.ts` and `fixtures/schedule-organization-fixture.ts`.
  - `packages/platform-objects` writes no `notify` node.
- **Test fixtures:** the notify tests in spec, lint and service-automation, the showcase's `approval-resume-relation-expand.test.ts` (its rolled-back shape is the CEL hop now; see Acceptance notes) and the translation-face and text-slot-list pins.
- **hotcrm** (read-only clone at `1d7148bf2d`, deleted after): 19 notify nodes in 15 flow files, each with one `{…}` recipient in a list (2 of them `{$User.Id}`), 35 `{…}` `templateData` values in 19 maps, and 19 links with holes (`/crm_lead/{record.id}`); no `sourceObject`, `sourceId`, `actorId` or `payload`. It is on `@objectstack/spec` 17.7.0, so nothing there moves until it upgrades.
- **objectui at the pin `4997995022`** (read-only), the designer's notify pickers, re-read at the pin (the stage-0 lines `:777`, `:856`, `:1103` are the S1/S2 `inputs`, `defaults` and `input` rows there now):
  - `flow-node-config.ts:1118`: `recipients` renders `FlowRecipientsField`, which writes a record-field row as `{record.FIELD}` (`FlowRecipientsField.tsx:106`) and reads a stored value with `readRecipients` (`:115`–`:118`), which keeps strings only — so a stored envelope entry, or a whole envelope, is dropped from the rows and lost on the next save.
  - `:1132` `sourceObject`, `:1133` `sourceId`, `:1139` `actionUrl`: `text` fields, whose default `refMode` is `template`, so the `{x}` picker inserts a single-brace token (`VariableTextInput.tsx`, `formatToken`). `:1120` `message`'s placeholder still reads "Supports {var} template references".
  - The descriptor publishes `recipients` untyped and the other keys with their `type`s, unchanged here, so `mergeServerFlowFields` keeps the hand-written picker and the pinned console still builds. No non-test objectui source imports `NotifyConfig`.
  - Carried to the objectui companion (objectstack-ai/objectui#12101) by the seat.

## Pins, and the ablations that turn them red

- `notify-value-slots.test.ts` (service-automation, 32 engine pins): each position refused at `registerFlow`, located and naming the envelope, and by the executor's contract parse as a guard; the recipient sentence; `actionUrl` refused with its hole spelling at both doors; each envelope evaluated, each literal handed on, a recipient string not split; the family finding (an entry evaluating to a list adds each recipient; never `'u1,u2'`); an absent variable fails with `EXECUTION_ERROR` naming `recipients[1]`; a guarded `null` is dropped; a node left with none fails naming the expressions; a map, and a list holding a number, fail the node naming them; `sourceId` `null` drops the pair and a map fails; `actionUrl` renders a hole, a map as JSON, and a link rendering nothing yields to the synthesized one.
- `notify-node.test.ts` re-judged in place: the interpolation fixtures move to envelopes and holes; the `framework#3582` trio now pins the guarded hop's `null` dropped, the node failing with the expression named, and the unguarded hop on a scalar id failing with `No such key: manager`.
- Spec: contract pins (`io-node-config.test.ts`: every position takes an envelope and a literal and refuses a token at its own path and a malformed envelope; a list mixes strings and envelopes and names the entry at fault; the build doors' value arm judges a list per element; the JSON projection carries the markers and keeps the literal arms; the describes); ledger pins (`flow-node-expression-paths.test.ts`: the six rows, `eachElement` on `recipients` only, element-by-element emission; the census row list); judge pins (`flow-value-slot-template.test.ts`: located per position, the recipient sentence and where it is absent); the text-slot list (`flow-text-slot-template.test.ts`); the translation face classifies `notify.actionUrl` (`flows-translation-face.test.ts`).
- The ratchet (`config-expression-ledger.test.ts`): notify declares its three slots on the spec Zod channel alone; `notify.recipients` joins the channel-required non-predicate slots refused absent.
- Lint: `validate-expressions.text-slot.test.ts` (envelopes pass, a token at the link is refused at `error`); `lint-flow-patterns.test.ts` (the double-brace control moves from `actionUrl`, a text slot now, to `sourceId`, a value slot).
- **Round 2, the literals.** The engine (`notify-value-slots.test.ts`, section 6, which replaces those keys' rows in sections 1 and 2): a literal is handed on as written, nested `payload` data included; a `{…}` token and an envelope are refused at `registerFlow` (located at the key, in the contract's words, with the literal remedy) and by the executor's contract parse as a guard. The contract (`io-node-config.test.ts`): a literal parses; a token is refused at its own path with the literal remedy, never the value slots' envelope; an envelope is refused; a token at any depth of a `payload` value is located at that string, and a deeper envelope is data; the build doors (`flowNodeConfigRefusals`, `FlowSchema.safeParse`) refuse a token and an envelope in the contract's words; the published JSON Schema keeps the 17.x shapes, with no marker and no envelope arm. `objectstack validate` (`validate-expressions.test.ts`) refuses both at `config.KEY` with the literal remedy, and a literal is clean. The lint hints (`lint-flow-patterns.test.ts`): the contract's literal keys, asked of the contract, are exactly the keys the hints read as literals, and a control key keeps its hint. The ledger, judge and ratchet pins count three notify slots.
- **Ablations**, at `384da59997`, each through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in WRAP mode under an outer `trap … EXIT INT TERM`: the anchor hit once, the blob changed, and the restore was proven with the blob equal to HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty (the outer check found nothing to restore).
  1. The executor's `recipients` reading restored to the 17.x `toStringList(interpolate(…))`: 8 of the 32 engine pins went red — every evaluation pin for `recipients`. The refusal pins stayed green, as they must: the contract parse refuses a token before the executor reads anything, so restoring the interpolator cannot reach them. (The dispatch predicted the refusal pins; the measured direction is the evaluation pins.)
  2. The ledger's `eachElement` deleted: 5 spec pins went red in 3 files (the element-wise emission, the located recipient refusal and its sentence, and the build doors' per-element value arm).
  3. The contract's token refusal for a list entry removed: 1 contract pin went red.
- Not ablated at dist level: the service-automation and lint pins read `@objectstack/spec`'s `dist`; ablations 2 and 3 turned the same functions red at source.
- **Round-2 ablations**, at `c200819d1e`, the same way (anchor hit once, blob changed, restore proven blob-equal to `HEAD`, `git diff HEAD` empty):
  4. The value arm's read-as-written line deleted (`flow-node-config-refusals.ts`): 3 of 73 pins in `io-node-config.test.ts` went red, exactly the three build-door pins (`sourceObject`, `actorId`, `payload`); the contract's own refusal pins stayed green.
  5. The contract's literal refusal removed (its `addIssue` replaced by `void refusal`): 8 of 73 went red: the three token refusals, the payload envelope, the payload depth case and the three build-door pins. The `sourceObject` / `actorId` envelope pins stayed green, as they must: the string type refuses those, not the refinement.

## Measurements

**Round 2, at `c200819d1e`** (the head; each suite took the verify lock once, on a shared box, so no wall-clock figure is an idle-box reading):

| run | result |
|:--|:--|
| the dependency closure build of service-automation and lint, spec included (`turbo run build --filter='…^...'`) | 29 tasks, exit 0 (after the dropped-refinements line moved: the first build refused, naming `automation/NotifyConfig` without `actorId` and `sourceObject`) |
| `@objectstack/service-automation`: the `notify-*` set (all six files) plus `config-expression-ledger` and `config-parse` | 8 files, 122 passed |
| `@objectstack/lint`: `lint-flow-patterns`, `validate-expressions`, `validate-expressions.text-slot` | 3 files, 640 passed |
| `@objectstack/spec` `vitest run --project local` (full) | 648 files, 19437 passed, 1 todo |
| `@objectstack/service-automation` `vitest run` (full) | 188 files, 2459 passed |
| `@objectstack/lint` `vitest run` (full) | 137 files, 6537 passed |
| `@objectstack/spec` / `service-automation` / `lint` `typecheck` | exit 0 each; the test layers OK against their debt ledgers (spec 52 / 246 / 135 held, service-automation 0, lint 2 / 6 / 2 held) |
| `check:generated`, `check:api-surface` ("public API surface + factory signatures unchanged"), `check:authorable-surface`, `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base origin/main` (`not-required (already-registered)`) | exit 0 each |

- **The gate union** at `c200819d1e`: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` with no paths derived 116 commands, and 115 were run. 113 exited 0 in the battery. `check:skill-examples` and `check:i18n-coverage` refused with exit 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET: `client-react` and the CLI and example closures were unbuilt in the re-created worktree). After the one closure build each names, both exited 0, and so did a re-run of `check:dts-closure`. Reconciled with `--ran`: "116 derived, 115 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 1 UNRUN"; the unrun one is `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, **NOT MEASURED** by the dispatch's rule.
- **⛔ crossed, reported:** the battery ran the derived `pnpm check:type-check-debt` (exit 0, "1 ledger entr(ies) re-measured … none above its recorded number"). That npm script is `--re-measure`, which the dispatch rules out, and it first runs the whole-workspace build `turbo run build --filter=./packages/* --filter=./packages/*/*`, outside the verify lock. That build rewrote `dist/` while my prerequisite build ran, so its first `client-react` declaration build failed (TS7016) and a `check:dts-closure` taken then named `verify`. Both were re-run green once it ended. Round 1's batteries ran the same script. The derivation tree was 8 commits behind `origin/main` (`51b43a8dc4`); 8 gate-input files changed there (workflows and ADR anchors), none of them in this diff.
- **ESLint, narrowed and proven**: `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 42 changed `.ts` files at `c200819d1e`: exit 0, 42 files in the JSON report, 0 errors, 0 warnings, none reported ignored. The config enables no type-aware linting (every `parserOptions` is `{ ecmaVersion: 'latest', sourceType: 'module' }`, no `project` / `projectService`; `eslint.config.mjs:327`–`:328`), so this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file. The whole-tree `pnpm lint` is CI's.
